 FAA Warns of Flight Delays at Major US Airports as Low Clouds and Strong Winds Disrupt Travel
 By 
Iuliia Tore 
 / Oct 26, 2026 / 3 minutes of reading Table of Contents
 Toggle Denver Faces Possible Ground Stop

 Strong Winds Could Slow Florida Airports 
 What US Air Travellers Should Know 
 Subscribe to our daily newsletter 
 Don't Miss A News 
 The Federal Aviation Administration has warned that low clouds and strong winds could disrupt flights at major US airports on Monday, October 26, including Chicago O’Hare, Denver, Seattle, San Francisco, Orlando and Miami. The weather conditions could reduce arrival capacity and lead to ground stops or delay programmes if visibility and runway conditions deteriorate.
 In its daily air traffic report, the FAA identified low clouds as a potential constraint at Chicago O’Hare (ORD), Chicago Midway (MDW), Denver (DEN), Detroit (DTW), San Francisco (SFO) and Seattle-Tacoma (SEA). Gusty winds could also slow traffic at several Florida airports, including Fort Lauderdale (FLL), Orlando (MCO), Miami (MIA) and Tampa (TPA).
 The FAA’s forecast identifies airports at risk of disruption rather than confirming that all listed airports are experiencing significant delays or cancellations.
 Denver Faces Possible Ground Stop 
 Denver International Airport is among the airports being closely monitored because of low cloud ceilings, which can limit the number of aircraft able to land during periods of reduced visibility.
 The FAA’s October 26 national operations plan identifies Denver as a potential candidate for a ground stop or ground delay programme if weather conditions reduce available capacity.
 The airport is also operating with Runway 16R/34L closed until November 5, according to the FAA’s published runway restrictions. The combination of reduced runway availability and low ceilings could complicate traffic management during busy periods.
 However, a possible ground stop is not the same as an active restriction. Passengers should check their individual flight status before assuming their departure or arrival has been affected.
 Chicago, Seattle and San Francisco Under Weather Watch 
 Low clouds could also affect operations at Chicago’s two major airports, O’Hare and Midway, as well as Detroit Metropolitan, Seattle-Tacoma and San Francisco International.
 When cloud ceilings fall, aircraft may require greater separation during approach, reducing the number of flights airports can accommodate each hour.
 Seattle is also operating with Runway 16C/34C closed until November 15, adding a separate infrastructure constraint to the day’s weather outlook.
 At San Francisco, the FAA has already listed a weather-related ground delay programme associated with low ceilings. Its operational summary recorded an average assigned delay of approximately 58 minutes for affected arrivals during the reporting period.
 Chicago O’Hare was separately reporting weather-related delays, although the available FAA summary did not establish a widespread cancellation event.

 Strong Winds Could Slow Florida Airports 
 In Florida, the FAA identified gusty winds as a potential operating constraint at Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International, Orlando International, Miami International and Tampa International.
 Strong crosswinds can reduce runway capacity or require changes to arrival and departure procedures. Flight delays may develop if weather conditions force air traffic controllers to reduce the rate at which aircraft can safely operate.
 The FAA’s national operations plan also identifies thunderstorms as a possible constraint across several air traffic control regions, including parts of Florida, Texas and the western United States.
 Additional routing restrictions may become necessary if storms affect major flight corridors.
 What US Air Travellers Should Know 
 The FAA has not announced a nationwide airport shutdown or confirmed widespread cancellations associated with the October 26 weather outlook.
 Passengers connecting through major hubs should nevertheless monitor both their departing flight and any onward connections, particularly where low visibility or strong winds could lead to air traffic restrictions.
 Travellers should check airline notifications for flight-specific information. FAA advisories provide airport-wide operating conditions and do not establish whether an individual flight will be delayed.
 The latest national outlook is available through the FAA Daily Air Traffic Report , while active restrictions can be checked through the FAA Air Traffic Control System Command Center .
